tagline: Self-hosted no-code workflow builder with TypeScript integrations, positioned as a Zapier replacement.
description: Activepieces is a visual automation tool. You chain a trigger and steps into a flow, with branches, loops, retries, HTTP calls and a code step that can use npm packages. Flows are versioned. Integrations are called pieces: npm packages written in TypeScript, and the project says community members wrote about 60 percent of them. You can build your own piece when a connector is missing. The pieces also work as MCP servers, so an LLM client such as Claude Desktop can call them. For self-hosting, the repository ships a Docker Compose file that starts the app, PostgreSQL (with the pgvector extension) and Redis. The docs list further install options. The Community Edition is MIT licensed, while enterprise features sit under a separate commercial licence, so check the pricing page before relying on a specific feature. It targets people who pay for Zapier or Make and want the same trigger-and-action model on their own server. Human approval steps and form or chat triggers are included. Expect a similar mental model to Zapier, so confirm that your key apps have a piece before migrating.
strengths: Flows support branches, loops, automatic retries, HTTP requests and a code step that can import npm packages
Every integration is an open-source TypeScript npm package, so a missing connector can be written and plugged in locally
Pieces double as MCP servers for LLM clients such as Claude Desktop, Cursor or Windsurf
Includes human-in-the-loop steps: delayed execution, approval requests, and form or chat interface triggers
Flows are fully versioned and the interface has translations
limits: The default Compose setup runs PostgreSQL and Redis alongside the app, so it is heavier than a single-container tool
Enterprise features are under a separate commercial licence, not the MIT Community Edition
The README counts 200+ pieces, so a niche app may have no connector and need a custom piece
Writing a missing integration means TypeScript development, not a settings screen
bestFor: A small team or agency that pays for Zapier, has a VPS, and wants its main app connections running on its own server.
